conclusion: Eight Codex-launched ripgrep context-discovery searches across six chats were scoped too broadly. Six completed orchestration cells printed only r.output, hiding command status/session metadata; another outer cell was explicitly terminated without stopping its native search. The owning chats moved on while searches remained alive.

verified_contributing_factors: Two content searches covered all of My Songs; others covered large Reports, Tools or multi-repository trees.
Blanket --hidden and inadequate generated-storage exclusions expanded discovery; actual output from the video-ID lookup contains .pnpm-store and many .tmp build/test paths.
The FFmpeg lookup searched every repository/worktree instead of the current owning checkout.
yield_time_ms and output caps limited waiting/display, not native search lifetime.
No search-exit verification was retained by the owners before moving on; the later cleanup checked native identities and verified all eight gone.

lifecycle_example.observation: The native rg process and pwsh wrapper survived the outer-cell termination and were found in the later process inventory.

uncertainty: No exact per-file I/O trace was available; Windows denied the earlier tracing attempt. Generated-tree traversal is directly evidenced, but its share of bytes/time is unknown.
This diagnoses agent command/lifecycle handling; it does not establish a specific app-server implementation bug or prove that a runtime defect was repaired.
The original commands searched My Songs, not necessarily every directory on the entire Z: volume.
No new storage-load measurements or sustained-performance-recovery claim were made.
Saving instructions does not prove receipt/adoption by every already-running chat.

limits: Positive rg inclusion globs and directly named paths can override ignores
PowerShell recursion does not use rgignore
Not evidence of adoption by an already-running command

changes.hard_limits: rgignore affects ordinary ripgrep discovery; direct paths, explicit overrides and other recursion tools require the shared scope/lifecycle rule. It is not a universal runtime block.

danceflow: Shared ecosystem guidance and discovery were consulted. The useful improvement is shared discovery policy plus ripgrep's native ignore primitive; no additional engine, model run or software release is justified.

media.omitted: No retrospective screenshot/video can prove the killed processes were alive. No live interface changed, and a new failure demonstration would be separate bounded work. The diagram is explicitly labelled as an illustration from retained evidence.
